Calf redness with pain or swelling (especially if unilateral) suggests possible deep vein thrombosis in low back pain. Most deep vein thromboses start in the deep veins of the calf and travel up the vascular system. Calf redness alone is not an indicator of deep vein thrombosis- consider together with calf pain, calf swelling, and predisposing risk factors to determine triage urgency.
